big_case.notes: Whether 12 U.S.C. § 248a(c)(2) removes regional Federal Reserve Banks' discretion under 12 U.S.C. § 342 to deny master accounts to eligible state-chartered nonmember institutions carries meaningful stakes for payment-system access, dual-banking federalism, and digital-asset banking, reflected in elite Supreme Court counsel, three cert-stage amicus briefs, and Judge Tymkovich's dissents below. However, there was no circuit split (the Tenth and Second Circuits agreed), Appointments Clause claims were held waived below, Custodia framed an all-or-nothing entitlement claim, Fed payment-account rulemaking reduced urgency, and certiorari was denied at first conference without relist or noted dissent.
